text: HTTPS is the first line of defense in web security, encrypting data between the user’s browser and the server. Without it, passwords and personal information can be intercepted by attackers. Authentication is equally important—using strong passwords and two-factor verification helps ensure that only authorized users gain access. Additionally, all user input must be validated and sanitized before it is processed. This prevents common vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS), where malicious code is inserted into forms or URLs. Regular security updates and testing are also essential. By combining these practices, developers can significantly reduce the risk of data breaches and keep their applications safe from attack.
